facts.fact: Senate ICT committee chair Shuaib Salisu said the National Digital Economy and E-Governance Bill, now at third reading, provides a regulatory framework for the responsible use of AI systems, categorises AI systems into four or five categories with different deployment requirements, and would apply to AI agents.
facts.system: National Digital Economy and E-Governance Bill

NGA.note: The document names no government body using an AI system.
The document names no AI tool in a public sector system.
The document names no AI model, dataset or AI computing built in Nigeria.

facts.fact: Senate ICT committee chair Shuaib Salisu said the National Digital Economy and E-Governance Bill, which would give electronic transactions, contracts and digital signatures the same legal weight as paper, had passed first and second readings and was at third reading, with assent expected in a few weeks.
facts.system: National Digital Economy and E-Governance Bill

NGA.note: The bill is said to mandate digitisation of government services, but the document does not say it provides for public bodies sharing data with each other.
